pcs.pc_description: mix paint as per specifications and in case of 2K system, mix base and hardener as per the recommended mixing ratio
perform the process of homogenising the paint in the container before preparing the paint for mixing base and hardener
prepare the mixed paint for application by adding the recommended thinner in the specified ratio
mix the thinned paint during application using an agitator (e.g., pneumatic stirrers - fit air driven agitator with pressure pot for continuous mixing during application)
use the homogenised material (mixed paint) within its pot life
select the correct application tool as per the SOP (e.g., brush, roller, air-assisted spray, airless spray gun)
check that the painting machine and airless spray gun is working properly
adjust the pressure and size of the orifice of the spray gun, for spraying paint
apply the paint on the surface - number of coats to be applied and the interval between coats should be as per SOP and/ or company’s standards
perform painting on the substrate with an airless spray gun as per product specification
determine wet film thickness
use anti-fouling paint on the bottom part of the ship, (which remains submerged in water) with an airless spray gun, as per product specification
cure the coating at the drying temperature and time recommended by the company’s standards/SOP
clean all application tools immediately after the application, as per company’s standards/SOP
dispose off contaminated residual solvent/ waste
visually inspect the dry painted surface for appearance and defects
check if the paint coat is even and without imperfections using recommended equipment
determine the dry film thickness
arrange for the repair of minor defects and repaint if required
compare the painted substrate with standards provided

pcs.pc_description: apply primer to provide excellent adhesion between the subsequent coatings (screed and top coat) and the floor
perform priming with the help of the recommended roller/squeezer, at the recommended coverage of kilograms per square meter
check if the total thickness developed through priming is well within permissible limits
ensure that the primer coat is allowed to cure at ambient temperature for 4-5 hours before application of the industrial screed
apply the screed layer within 24 hours of curing of the primer
ensure that the base, hardener, and aggregate are uniformly and slowly mixed using a slow speed stirrer
practise adding the base component, followed by the hardener and mix them for 2 minutes to obtain an even colour
perform the addition of filler pack to the base- hardener mixture and mix for 3 minutes to obtain a uniform mix
apply the screed mix immediately after mixing, by spreading it evenly over the recommended area using a steel trowel with notches
remove entrapped air with the help of a spike roller with long handle, after the screed application as well as after topcoat application
ensure that the screed is allowed to cure at ambient temperature for up to 5-8 hours to obtain the desired strength for the subsequent application
apply an intermediate coat / scratch coat to avoid any pinholes, waviness, etc.
remove undue protrusions/undulations from the cured screed coat with the help of sanding/ grinding methods
ensure that the pigment paste is added to the base at the factory to avoid mixing errors at the site
perform the mixing of base, pigment paste, hardener, and aggregate uniformly using a slow- speed mixer with a paddle attachment
apply the top coat mix, immediately after mixing, by spreading it evenly over the recommended area using a steel trowel with notches
check if the floor coating settles to an even coloured, aesthetically appealing, impervious floor
examine if the floor coating has been allowed to cure at ambient temperature for at least 24 hours
inspect the floor for visible defects/flaws like blisters, bubbles or pinholes
repair flaws by grinding the flaw area and up to 5 cm from the flaw area to the substrate level

pcs.pc_description: check the ambient % relative humidity and temperature suitability for the process
inspect the substrate/ surface for oil/grease, dirt, salt or white patches/ rust and imperfections
check the durability of scaffolding for personal safety and obtain approval on it from the competent authority
identify the materials in the surroundings to be masked before preparation and painting
check the adhesion of previously applied coating onto the surface
identify the factors (type of substrate/ floor, type of contamination, desired cleaning grade, surface profile, etc.) that determine the type of surface preparation required for the substrate/ floor
compare various types of surface preparation methods like washing (with detergent and water), grinding, scarifying, vacuum blast cleaning, acid etching, etc.
mask the materials in the surroundings that do not require painting
clean the surface with the help of chemicals -to free it of oil/grease, dirt, rust, soil, salts, and other contaminants
prepare the surface for painting using wire brush, chipping tool, power tool, hydro or abrasive blast machines
perform sealing of cracks/crevices/joints on the floor to prevent water seepage
patch the cracks by widening the cracks to a sufficient size and to a depth of 1–2 cm, using an angle grinder and a compatible filler compound

arrange for the repair of large (>5mm in depth) cracks, holes, and joints with the help of a solvent- less and colourless epoxy topcoat, mixed with a sufficient quantity of dry natural sand of suitable grain size

select the appropriate surface preparation method based on the type of the substrate/ floor (natural/Kota/Kadapa stone type/tile/marble/concrete/mosaic), the level difference or undulations on the substrate/ floor, the level of smoothness, etc.
clean the previously coated floors with the help of detergent solution in case of mild contamination of dust or dirt or with the help of scarifying method in case of deep-seated oil contamination
remove previously applied coating mechanically in case of poor adhesion
clean the surface by sweeping or vacuum cleaning after surface preparation to remove any sanding residue/ dust
perform coving of corners using a mix of natural sand and solvent-less epoxy or an epoxy- based coving compound
check whether all imperfections have been treated
check whether the surface profile is as per the product specification
perform pre-inspection of the surface before applying the coating
check if the floor to be coated has a minimum pull-off adhesion strength of 1.5N/mm2 and a compressive strength of at least 25 N/mm2
ensure that the floor has matured for a minimum of 28-42 days in ambient conditions before coating
examine the moisture content of the floor, using either a moisture meter or by taping a 1.2 m x 1.2 m plastic sheet to the floor
check if there is any ingress of water through cracks/crevices/ joints in the substrate/ floor
ensure that the floor/ surface temperature is 3°C above the determined dew point in order to avoid moisture condensation
check if the floor/ surface temperature ranges between 10° - 40°C
perform the marking of joint positions on the floor
